name: Belarus
summary: Extremely harsh. Possessing any amount, even for own use, is a crime (up to 5 yrs). Selling: 3–8 yrs, 6–15 yrs if aggravated, up to 25 yrs if a death results. Analogues are covered too.

emergency.poisonControlNote: No public poison hotline could be verified; call 103 (ambulance).

callingForHelp: No legal protection. Police are often involved in drug-related medical cases and any possession is a crime. Handing over drugs and actively helping police can exempt (CC art. 328 note).
drugChecking: No drug checking services exist; harm reduction services are very limited.

uk.title: Criminal Code of Belarus, arts. 328, 328-1, 328-2, 329 (pravo.by, as amended to 2025)

un1971.title: INCB Green List: psychotropic substances under international control (1971 Convention)

wikiCannabis.title: Wikipedia: Legality of cannabis (Belarus: illegal for all uses)

lsd.note: Possession of any amount without intent to sell: arrest, restricted freedom up to 5 yrs, or 2–5 yrs in prison.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is controlled; possessing any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs). Growing fungi containing drugs: up to 3 yrs.

dmt.note: UN Schedule I; possession of any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs). Ayahuasca contains DMT.

mescaline.note: UN Schedule I; possession of any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs).

dox.note: DOB, DOM, DOC are UN-scheduled; possession of any amount is a crime.

nbomes.note: 25I/25B/25C-NBOMe are UN Schedule I and analogues are also covered; possession of any amount is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other 2C-x are UN-scheduled and analogues are covered; possession of any amount is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are UN Schedule I; possession of any amount is a crime.

5-meo-xxt.note: The Criminal Code also covers drug 'analogues', so 5-MeO tryptamines are very likely prosecuted like listed drugs (up to 5 yrs).

cannabis.note: Possession of any amount: up to 5 yrs. Growing cannabis to obtain drugs: up to 3 yrs. Repeat public use within a year is also a crime. No medical use.

ketamine.note: Controlled anaesthetic. Possession without a prescription is likely prosecuted like other controlled drugs (up to 5 yrs).

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is UN Schedule II; possession of any amount is a crime.

dxm.note: Not internationally controlled; its national status and pharmacy rules in Belarus could not be verified.

nitrous.note: Could not verify whether nitrous oxide is restricted. Being intoxicated by 'stupefying substances' in public is an offence.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine: possession of any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs); selling 3–15 yrs.

mdma.note: UN Schedule I; possession of any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs).

cocaine.note: Possession of any amount is a crime (up to 5 yrs). Bringing drugs across the border: 3–7 yrs.

caffeine.note: Legal and not a controlled substance.

alcohol.note: Legal from 18; sale to minors is prohibited and public drunkenness is an offence.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is UN Schedule II; possession of any amount is a crime. Status of GBL/1,4-BD not verified.

opioids.note: Heroin and fentanyl-type drugs: possession of any amount is a crime; 'especially dangerous' drugs raise selling penalties. Rx opioids: prescription only.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine; whether it is on Belarus's controlled lists was not verified.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only, UN Schedule IV psychotropics; possession without a prescription can be prosecuted.

maois.note: Pharmaceutical MAOIs are prescription-only. The status of harmala/Syrian rue was not verified; DMT in ayahuasca is illegal.
